name: Curie Uniformity Detection (Length CV)
description: Calculates the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of sentence lengths to mathematically expose the unnatural structural uniformity typical of machine generation.
algorithm: Sentence Length Coefficient of Variation (CV) Profiling
mechanism: The 'Curie' detection profile focuses on a fundamental byproduct of autoregressive text generation: structural homogenization. Large Language Models continuously balance attention weights to produce text that flows smoothly and minimizes immediate perplexity. A mathematical consequence of this safe pathfinding is that the lengths of generated sentences converge violently toward a narrow median. By calculating the Coefficient of Variation (CV)—the standard deviation of sentence lengths divided by the mean—this method quantifies the textual rhythm. Human writers instinctively mix ultra-short, punchy sentences with long, sprawling, multi-clause explanations to manipulate pacing and emphasis, resulting in a high CV. In contrast, AI generators inevitably slip into a hypnotic rhythm of medium-length sentences, lacking both the extreme brevity and extreme length found in natural human thought processes. A pathologically low sentence length CV strongly indicates synthetic smoothing.
useCase: Analyzing essays, reports, and long-form prose where the relentless, hypnotic pacing of medium-length AI sentences betrays a lack of human narrative rhythm.
strengths:
• Computationally lightweight but highly lethal; uses fundamental math rather than complex neural networks.
• Extremely difficult for basic AI generators to overcome natively, as their inherent training forces them toward syntactic averaging.
• Language-agnostic, functioning perfectly on any language that uses defined sentence boundary punctuation.
limitations:
• Requires a substantial text fragment (minimum 10-15 sentences) to calculate a statistically meaningful standard deviation and mean.
• False positives can occur in highly regulated, formulaic human writing (e.g., technical manuals or simplified children's books) designed for absolute consistency.
• Prompt engineers can bypass this by explicitly demanding varying sentence lengths (e.g., 'Use a mix of 3-word and 30-word sentences').
parameters:
Analysis: Sentence Boundary Tokenization & Statistical Profiling
Metric: Coefficient of Variation (Standard Deviation / Mean Sentence Length)
Output: 0-100 Structural Homogenization (Rhythm Deficit) Score
accuracy: High — 75-85%. Particularly devastating against unfiltered, default-temperature outputs from models like GPT-3.5 and Claude.

references.title: Sadasivan, V. S. et al. (2023). Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected? arXiv.
Ippolito, D. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Generated Text is Easiest when Humans are Fooled. ACL.
